speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the location and severity of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as blood or increased frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any burning sensation, urgency, or frequency when urinating during or after your sinus infection treatment? I also need to know which specific antibiotic you were prescribed for the sinusitis.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash appear shortly after starting amoxicillin, and have you experienced any joint pain, abdominal pain, or changes in your urine color since then? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_morphology

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated eosinophils in your urine strongly suggests an allergic reaction to your medication. Did you notice any swelling of your face, lips, or tongue, or have you experienced any shortness of breath since starting the antibiotics?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, flank pain, eosinophiluria, and a prior rash after antibiotic exposure is classic for Acute Interstitial Nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
